comparisons.peer_topic: Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) Requirements and Compliance
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation must maintain a minimum SLR of 3.0% plus a 2.0% leverage buffer to avoid restrictions on capital distributions and bonus payments, with the numerator defined as quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital and the denominator based on total leverage exposure. At December 31, 2024, its insured depository institution subsidiaries exceeded the 6.0% minimum SLR required to be considered well capitalized under the PCA framework.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose leverage ratio compliance and composition details. GS highlights that pending profits contributed 87 basis points to its leverage ratio. BAC details its Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) requirements, noting the need to maintain a minimum SLR of 3.0% plus a 2.0% buffer to avoid distribution restrictions, and confirms its subsidiaries exceeded the 6.0% minimum for well-capitalized status. Both address the mechanics and thresholds of leverage metrics, though GS focuses on profit inclusion and BAC on regulatory minimums and buffer status.

sentences.text: These profits contributed 87 basis points to the leverage ratio as of December 2024.

The Corporation is also required to maintain a minimum supplementary leverage ratio (SLR) of 3.0 percent plus a leverage buffer of 2.0 percent in order to avoid certain restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments to executive officers.
At December 31, 2024, our insured depository institution subsidiaries exceeded their requirement to maintain a minimum 6.0 percent SLR to be considered well capitalized under the PCA framework.
